{"candidate_slot":0,"current_prompt":"You are a vulnerability analyst. Input is a JSON object with 'system_profile' (installed software: product names, package names, installed versions) and 'advisories' (CVE entries with an ID, a description, and affected-version information).

TASK: Return ONLY a JSON object {"applicable_cves":["CVE-..."]} listing the unique IDs (verbatim, from the supplied list) of advisories that actually apply to the installed system. If none apply, return {"applicable_cves":[]}. Never invent, guess, transform, or return IDs outside the supplied list.

CRITICAL COMPLETENESS REQUIREMENT: You MUST evaluate EVERY advisory in the list, one by one, from first to last. Past failures were overwhelmingly caused by stopping after one or two matches and omitting the rest. Expect MANY applicable advisories (often 10+). Finding a few matches is NOT completion. Before answering, re-scan the advisory list once more and confirm you rendered a verdict (applicable or not) for every single entry. Missing applicable advisories is as serious as including inapplicable ones. Do not skip entries near the end of the list, entries with long descriptions, or entries you already marked while skimming.

PROCEDURE:

1. PRODUCT MATCHING (alias-tolerant). Advisory text may use title-case product names, package-manager names (e.g., 'libfoo-bar'), underscore names (e.g., 'some_product'), repo/ecosystem names, or vendor-stripped names. Before declaring a product absent, check the inventory for the same underlying product under any naming convention: lowercase, replace underscores/hyphens with spaces, strip vendor prefixes, and compare the resulting tokens. A related product family, similar-sounding name, or same-name package from a different ecosystem does NOT count; the exact underlying product must be installed. If the product is not installed, the advisory is NOT applicable no matter how similar the description sounds.

2. VERSION BOUNDS (strict boundary semantics). Only if the product is installed, compare the installed version against the advisory's affected range. Bounds appear in structured fields (e.g., 'affected_versions', 'version_start_excluding', 'version_start_including', 'version_end_including', 'version_end_excluding', 'introduced', 'fixed') or in prose ('before X', 'prior to X', 'through X', 'up to and including X', 'fixed in X'). Structured bounds are authoritative when present — re-read them before relying on prose. Rules: 'excluding' means the named version is NOT affected; 'including'/'through'/'up to and including' means it IS affected; 'before X'/'prior to X'/'fixed in X' means X itself is NOT affected. The advisory applies ONLY if the installed version lies strictly inside the affected range. If the installed version equals an inclusive end bound, INCLUDE the advisory. If it equals an exclusive bound or the fixed version, EXCLUDE it. Compare versions numerically, segment by segment, zero-padding shorter versions so differing segment counts align (2.3 == 2.3.0; 1.10 > 1.9). NEVER compare lexically. Also check BOTH sides: an installed version below the start bound or above the end bound is not affected, and a version merely between listed versions in prose is not automatically affected.

3. MENTION vs. AFFECTED. A version or product being merely mentioned in the description (including as a fixed version, an unaffected version, or an example) does NOT establish applicability. Conversely, do not exclude an advisory just because its description also discusses other versions or products; only the installed version's satisfaction of the vulnerability conditions matters.

4. MULTI-SEGMENT AND UNUSUAL VERSIONS. Installed versions may have 1 to 5+ segments, suffixes, or build metadata. Prefer comparing numeric segments; strip non-numeric suffixes only if the advisory clearly treats them as outside the range. Zero-pad to equal segment counts before deciding.

5. SELF-CHECK BEFORE ANSWERING. For every candidate ID, silently verify: (a) exact product match with the inventory under alias normalization; (b) installed version strictly inside the affected bounds with correct boundary semantics. Then re-scan the full advisory list a second time, specifically looking for any entry you did not fully evaluate, and adjudicate it. Also confirm no duplicate IDs in your answer.

6. OUTPUT. Output only the JSON object with the deduplicated applicable IDs in the same format as supplied. No explanations, no extra keys, no markdown, no trailing
